question: A statue that is 1.6 meters in height is positioned on top of a pedestal. From a location on the ground, the angle of elevation to the top of the statue measures 60 degrees, while the angle of elevation to the top of the pedestal from the same point is 45 degrees. Determine the height of the pedestal.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of lower part (h) = Height of upper part (d) ÷ [tan(higher angle) ÷ tan(lower angle) − 1]

Given d = 1.6 m, higher angle = 60°, lower angle = 45°

h = 1.6 ÷ (tan 60° ÷ tan 45° − 1) = 1.6 ÷ (√3 ÷ 1 − 1) = 1.6 ÷ (√3 − 1)

Rationalizing the denominator: h = 1.6 × (√3 + 1) ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

h = 1.6(√3 + 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = 0.8(√3 + 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 0.8(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ In right-angled triangle BCD, tan 45° = BC ÷ CD

⇒ 1 = h ÷ x

⇒ x = h

⇒ In right-angled triangle ACD, tan 60° = AC ÷ CD

⇒ √3 = (AB + BC) ÷ x

⇒ √3 = (1.6 + h) ÷ h

⇒ h√3 = 1.6 + h

⇒ h(√3 − 1) = 1.6

⇒ h = 1.6 ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator: h = 1.6(√3 + 1) ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

⇒ h = 1.6(√3 + 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = 0.8(√3 + 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 0.8(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Values

Standard trigonometric ratios frequently used in heights and distances: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

Rationalization of Surds

To simplify an expression of the form a / (√b − c), multiply both the numerator and the denominator by its conjugate (√b + c) to eliminate the square root from the denominator.

Angle of Elevation

It is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is viewed from below. A higher angle of elevation corresponds to a greater vertical height for objects observed from the same horizontal distance.
